_provenance.written_in_session: From 2026-09-30, from public sources only (listed under each place); no API batch (AGENTS.md).
_provenance.rules: Plain English, no praise words, figures only where a listed source publishes them, never 'official boundary' (spec §18). Exactly one key fact 'Established YYYY (27 CFR 9.N)', as TTB lists it. Descriptions of 2-4 sentences, at most 700 characters. At most 8 grapes; the 1-3 signature grapes are PRINCIPAL and the rest ACCESSORY. At least two sources per place, one of them the CFR section or the Federal Register final rule. share_pct is left out.

article.description: A small, high valley of about 1,440 acres in southwestern Lake County, at about 2,400 feet among mountains averaging 2,800 feet. Its only commercial vineyard was the Trione family's Chardonnay, grown for Geyser Peak; the harsh climate defeated it, most vines were removed, and the valley is now mainly grazing land. It is named after Benjamin Logan Moore, a 19th-century cattle rustler.
article.climate: Cold for California: the growing season starts late, the average last frost comes in late May, and frost has been recorded as late as the Fourth of July.
article.soils: Soils of an enclosed mountain valley floor and its surrounding slopes.
article.grape_varieties: Chardonnay was the only grape grown commercially here.
article.wine_styles: Dry white wine from Chardonnay, when the vineyard was farmed.
key_facts: About 1,440 acres at about 2,400 feet (Lake County News)
Named after Benjamin Logan Moore (Lake County News)

article.description: The flat valley floor south of Clear Lake around Kelseyville and Finley, about 11,000 acres between about 1,300 and 1,550 feet. At establishment it had 43 vineyards with about 1,800 acres of grapes and six wineries, and it holds most of Lake County's Sauvignon Blanc.
article.climate: Lakeside and high, at about 1,300 to 1,550 feet, with Clear Lake moderating temperatures.
article.soils: Mostly alluvial soils laid down on the lake's old floodplain, with seams of gravel.
article.grape_varieties: Sauvignon Blanc above all, with Cabernet Sauvignon, Zinfandel, Cabernet Franc and Chardonnay.
article.wine_styles: Dry Sauvignon Blanc and red wines from Cabernet Sauvignon and Zinfandel.
key_facts: 43 vineyards with about 1,800 acres of grapes at establishment (TTB final rule)

article.description: A bench of about 9,100 acres west of Kelseyville, between the volcanic mountains around Mount Konocti and the flat Big Valley below, from about 1,400 to 1,775 feet. At establishment it had 27 vineyards with about 900 acres of grapes and one winery.
article.climate: High and inland, with warm days and cool nights, between the volcanic uplands and the lake plain.
article.soils: Once a pyroclastic flow, the bench is a transition from volcanic mountains to alluvial plain: rocky volcanic soils with good drainage, giving smaller crops.
article.grape_varieties: Cabernet Sauvignon and Zinfandel, with Cabernet Franc, Sauvignon Blanc and Merlot.
article.wine_styles: Dry red wines from Cabernet Sauvignon, Zinfandel and Cabernet Franc, and some whites.
key_facts: 27 vineyards with about 900 acres of grapes at establishment (TTB final rule)
Lies within the Clear Lake AVA

article.description: A valley of about 17,360 acres at the north end of Clear Lake around the town of Upper Lake, between 1,300 and 1,800 feet. At establishment it had 16 commercial vineyards on about 300 acres. The same rule moved the Clear Lake boundary so that it lies wholly within it.
article.climate: About 3,158 growing degree days (median), about 202 frost-free days and 35 to 43 inches of rain a year; constant gentle winds keep canopies cool and dry.
article.soils: Moderately deep loams on the hills, deep loams on the valley floor, and poorly drained silty clay loams, over a shallow, calcium-rich groundwater basin.
article.grape_varieties: Sauvignon Blanc, the grape the rule names, with Cabernet Sauvignon.
article.wine_styles: Dry Sauvignon Blanc and some red wine from Cabernet Sauvignon.
key_facts: About 17,360 acres; 16 vineyards on about 300 acres at establishment (TTB final rule)
Rainfall 35 to 43 inches a year (TTB final rule)

article.description: A very small AVA, about 150 acres on a single ranch in the hills between Ukiah and Boonville in Mendocino County, at about 1,400 to 1,600 feet. Its vineyard grows Cabernet Sauvignon, Riesling, Pinot Noir and Merlot.
article.climate: An upland climate at about 1,400 to 1,600 feet, in the hills between the coast and the warm inland valleys.
article.soils: Upland soils on the ranch's slopes and small valley floor.
article.grape_varieties: Cabernet Sauvignon and Riesling, with Pinot Noir and Merlot.
article.wine_styles: Dry red wines from Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot, and Riesling.
key_facts: About 150 acres at establishment (Wine Institute, from the TTB final rule)
A single ranch between Ukiah and Boonville

article.description: A low valley of about 1,422 acres in coastal Mendocino County, around the hamlet of Comptche, surrounded by forest and short, steep ridges. TTB kept it out of the North Coast AVA because its climate and soils differ. At establishment three vineyards grew over 30 acres, all of it Pinot Noir.
article.climate: Cool: about 2,259 growing degree days, and vineyards between 220 and 250 feet in a valley from 187 to 400 feet.
article.soils: Shallow, well-drained, infertile Bearwallow-Wolfey soils over fractured sandstone, and deep, clay-rich Perrygulch loam on the bottomland.
article.grape_varieties: Pinot Noir is the only grape grown commercially.
article.wine_styles: Dry Pinot Noir from a handful of vineyards.
key_facts: About 1,421.8 acres, outside the North Coast AVA (T.D. TTB-192)
Three vineyards covering over 30 acres at establishment (T.D. TTB-192)

article.description: A mountainous AVA of about 26,260 acres in Mendocino County, west of Redwood Valley, named after the Eagle Peak summit. At establishment about 120 acres were planted in 16 vineyards, mostly Pinot Noir; Masút, farmed by the Fetzer brothers, is among them.
article.climate: Cool growing-season temperatures with a marine influence and strong breezes.
article.soils: Shallow soils with little water-holding capacity on steep slopes, unlike the deep alluvial soils of the valleys around it.
article.grape_varieties: Pinot Noir dominates the small planted area.
article.wine_styles: Dry Pinot Noir from steep mountain vineyards.
key_facts: About 120 acres in 16 vineyards at establishment (T.D. TTB-124)

article.description: A valley of about 4,396 acres in southern Lake County, one of the earliest AVAs. The actress Lillie Langtry bought the Guenoc ranch in 1888 to make claret-style wine, and the estate still farms Cabernet Sauvignon and the other Bordeaux varieties.
article.climate: A rain-shadowed inland valley shut off by rocky ridges, with warm days and cool nights.
article.soils: Soils of the valley floor and the rocky ridges around it.
article.grape_varieties: Cabernet Sauvignon and the other Bordeaux varieties, with Sauvignon Blanc.
article.wine_styles: Dry red wines from Cabernet Sauvignon and Bordeaux blends, and dry whites.
key_facts: About 4,396 acres at establishment (Wine Institute, from the TTB final rule)
Lillie Langtry bought the Guenoc ranch in 1888 (The Seattle Times)

article.description: An enclosed, bowl-shaped valley of about 14,000 acres above the eastern shore of Clear Lake near Clearlake Oaks, running east to west, which is unusual in the Coast Ranges. Its floor lies at 1,700 to 1,800 feet and the AVA reaches 3,000 feet. About 1,000 acres were planted at establishment.
article.climate: Region 2–3, one of the cooler parts of Lake County: winds from the Clear Lake basin blow through the valley, frost can come into June, and rain varies from about 18 to 35 inches.
article.soils: Weathered volcanic residue and Franciscan sandstone and shale: Wolfcreek loam on the valley floor, Millsholm and Hopland series on the ridges.
article.grape_varieties: Cabernet Sauvignon and Sauvignon Blanc, with Syrah, Zinfandel, Merlot and Petite Sirah.
article.wine_styles: Dry red wines from Cabernet Sauvignon and Syrah, and dry Sauvignon Blanc.
key_facts: About 14,000 acres, about 1,000 planted at establishment (T.D. TTB-30)

sources.title: 27 CFR 9.189, High Valley (eCFR text via Cornell LII)

article.description: A long, narrow valley of about 7,605 acres in eastern Lake County, with a floor at about 1,322 feet and foothills rising 200 to 500 feet more. At establishment it had five vineyards on about 149 acres and three wineries; the same rule extended High Valley to meet it.
article.climate: Region III, about 3,378 growing degree days: wind through the valley cools the vines, and cold air draining off the foothills protects them from late spring frost; 27 to 33 inches of rain.
article.soils: Soils of the Cache Formation: tuffaceous and diatomaceous sands and silts, limestone, gravel and volcanic rocks.
article.grape_varieties: Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc, Petite Sirah and Syrah.
article.wine_styles: Dry red wines from Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc, Petite Sirah and Syrah.
key_facts: Five vineyards on about 149 acres and three wineries at establishment (T.D. TTB-188)

sources.title: 27 CFR 9.289, Long Valley-Lake County (eCFR text via Cornell LII)

article.description: A small valley east of Hopland in Mendocino County, ringed by mountains, known for some of the oldest Syrah and Grenache in California. The first varietal Syrah released in California came from these vines, from the 1978 vintage. Cold air gathers on the valley floor at night.
article.climate: Warm days and cool nights: cold air collects on the enclosed valley floor after dark, which keeps acidity in the grapes.
article.soils: Soils of the valley floor and benches, dry-farmed in the old blocks.
article.grape_varieties: Syrah and Grenache, with Petite Sirah, in old head-trained, dry-farmed blocks.
article.wine_styles: Dry red wines from Syrah and Grenache, and dry rosé.
key_facts: California's first varietal Syrah came from here, the 1978 vintage (Historic Vineyard Society)

sources.title: 27 CFR 9.36, McDowell Valley (eCFR text via Cornell LII)

article.description: A high valley of about 27,500 acres at the headwaters of the East Fork of the Russian River in Mendocino County, at about 1,000 feet, roughly twice the height of Ukiah. Guinness McFadden settled here in 1970 and began planting Riesling, now its signature grape.
article.climate: Continental for Mendocino: days can reach 95 °F and nights fall to the 40s or low 50s; the height gives a shorter season, later budbreak and earlier frosts.
article.soils: Soils of the upland valley floor at the river's headwaters.
article.grape_varieties: Riesling first, with Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Noir, Pinot Gris and Gewürztraminer.
article.wine_styles: Dry and off-dry Riesling, dry Sauvignon Blanc and Pinot Noir.
key_facts: About 27,500 acres at establishment (Wine Institute, from the TTB final rule)

article.description: An upland valley of about 22,400 acres north of Ukiah in the east-central interior of Mendocino County. Italian immigrant families planted some of the county's early vineyards here, and it is known for Zinfandel, Cabernet Sauvignon, Petite Sirah and Carignan.
article.climate: Cooler than the surrounding inland areas because a gap in the coastal ridge lets Pacific air in; ripening is gradual.
article.soils: Thin, rocky, iron-rich red soils on the valley floor and slopes.
article.grape_varieties: Zinfandel and Cabernet Sauvignon, with Petite Sirah, Carignan and Barbera.
article.wine_styles: Dry red wines from Zinfandel, Cabernet Sauvignon and Petite Sirah.
key_facts: About 22,400 acres at establishment (Wine Institute, from the TTB final rule)

sources.title: 27 CFR 9.153, Redwood Valley (eCFR text via Cornell LII)

article.description: A string of high benches and troughs along Highway 128 in southern Mendocino County, between Anderson Valley and Alexander Valley, following the headwaters of Dry Creek and Rancheria Creek. Of about 40,000 acres, some 70 were planted at establishment, almost entirely above 800 feet.
article.climate: In between Anderson Valley and Alexander Valley: about 3,060 heat units against 2,500 and 3,650 there, with marine air more than half the growing season and about 50 inches of rain.
article.soils: Rocky hill soils with gravel and old brittle rock, thinner than their neighbours': Bearwallow, Hellman and Yorkville series.
article.grape_varieties: Pinot Noir and Sauvignon Blanc, with Chardonnay and Syrah.
article.wine_styles: Dry Pinot Noir and Sauvignon Blanc, and some Syrah.
key_facts: About 40,000 acres; about 70 planted at establishment (T.D. ATF-397)
The same rule extended the Mendocino AVA to take it in (T.D. ATF-397)

article.description: A small valley in southwestern Solano County, about four miles long and one mile wide, next to the Napa County line and west of Suisun Valley. It is not the Green Valley in Sonoma County. About 800 acres are planted, mostly to red grapes.
article.climate: Maritime, moderated by nearby Suisun Bay.
article.soils: Soils of the small valley floor and its surrounding slopes.
article.grape_varieties: Cabernet Sauvignon, Zinfandel and Petite Sirah, with Sangiovese, Syrah and Merlot.
article.wine_styles: Dry red wines from Cabernet Sauvignon, Zinfandel and Petite Sirah.
key_facts: About 2,560 acres at establishment (Wine Institute, from the TTB final rule)

article.description: A valley about 8 miles long and 3 miles wide in Solano County, east of Napa, of about 15,000 acres with some 3,000 planted. It was first known for Cabernet Sauvignon and Petite Sirah and now grows more than 20 varieties; just over a dozen wineries work here.
article.climate: Region III, with marine air from the Pacific and San Pablo Bay flowing in; the southern end can be up to 14 °F cooler.
article.soils: Soils of the valley floor and the surrounding foothills.
article.grape_varieties: Cabernet Sauvignon and Petite Sirah, with Syrah, Zinfandel, Chardonnay and Sauvignon Blanc.
article.wine_styles: Dry red wines from Petite Sirah and Cabernet Sauvignon, and dry whites.
key_facts: About 15,000 acres, some 3,000 planted (The Bubbly Professor)
